issues.body: The workflow creates `BINDING_REF` at lines 978–986 and only afterward runs `gh secret set` at line 991. If that write fails without storing the credential, the binding survives. A later out-of-band write to the same environment-secret name makes `probe_secret` succeed, and reconciliation then emits `resume=true` / `stage=register`, registering an account around a credential this enrollment never captured. Moving the absence probes before the binding excludes only writes visible before binding creation; it cannot distinguish a successful store from a failed store followed by a later write. The added tests exercise binding followed by an absence-probe refusal, but that probe now necessarily precedes the binding; they still omit the provenance-breaking transition required in round 4.
issues.fix_hint: Add durable protocol state that distinguishes capture intent from capture completion and permit `stage=register` only when completion is attributable to this enrollment. Add an executable test for `binding created -> gh secret set fails -> secret absent -> out-of-band secret created -> retry` and require refusal. If the secret API cannot provide an atomic or identity-bound completion proof, make the ambiguous pre-store-binding state manual-recovery-only instead of inferring completion from secret existence.
issues.title: The pre-store binding still cannot attribute a later secret to this enrollment

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 5 hardens the binding parser and correctly moves both absence probes ahead of binding creation, but it still does not resolve round 4's credential-provenance defect. The durable binding remains published before `gh secret set`, and reconciliation still treats later secret existence as proof that this enrollment completed the write. If `gh secret set` fails after the binding is created and an out-of-band writer subsequently creates the named secret, the next retry emits `resume=true` and `stage=register` around that unrelated credential. The new tests call a probe-before-binding refusal “the transition,” but they do not execute the prior round's required sequence: binding created, store fails, secret is absent, out-of-band secret appears, retry. The same major finding remains, so progress is stagnant.
